name: Ministry of Supply
why: Boston company from MIT that makes dress shirts, blazers and suits in performance knits; its stores are closed while it moves, with a dozen live styles.
origin: Founded in 2012 in Cambridge, Massachusetts, US by Aman Advani, Gihan Amarasiriwardena, Kevin Rustagi, Kit Hickey.

craft_evidence.owned: none evidenced: brand claims 'Ministry Production Systems ... on-demand, waste-free manufacturing' (2025, Our Story) but names no facility; PDPs name contract maker Lever Style in China
craft_evidence.makers: evidence (PDPs): 'Made by Lever Style' Shenzhen / Dongguan, China on 10 of 12 men's styles read; previous-gen Velocity jacket 'Made by Matsuoka (Pinghu, CN) and Toray-TGE (Bangkok, TH)'
craft_evidence.mills: none: PDPs name fibre trademarks (Primeflex®, Solotex®, Sorona) but no mill; fabric-technology page names no supplier
craft_evidence.heritage: dated and placed (claim): Our Story timeline '2011 — Born at MIT', 'Born in Cambridge raised in the labs of MIT'; 2012 Apollo shirt Kickstarter
craft_evidence.process: partial: fabric performance claims (phase-change, warp-knit stretch, laser-cut aeration) on fabric-technology page; no description of how garments are made
craft_evidence.reasoning: Product pages name the maker (Lever Style, Shenzhen/Dongguan) on 10 of 12 men's styles and state China as origin on 11 of 12, but the brand owns no facility it shows and names no mill. Its own pages document fabric performance, not making; the 'Ministry Production Systems' on-demand claim names no place.

ownership.owner: private, venture-backed (2013 $1.1M seed from VegasTechFund, SK Ventures, Craig Breslow per TechCrunch via Wikipedia); later rounds/current cap table not establ
